chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subbah al-Kinanī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a woman who freed a man, [asking] for whom is his walayah and for whom is his inheritance? He said: 'For the one who freed him, unless he has an heir other than her.'
ai.seo_question: Who inherits the freed slave and holds the right of walayah when a woman manumits a male slave?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the right of manumission (walayah) and inheritance generally belongs to the person who frees the slave, unless a closer kinship tie exists with another heir. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle that walayah is not exclusive to the manumitter but is subject to the broader hierarchy of inheritance, ensuring that familial bonds take precedence over the contractual act of freeing. It underscores the integration of manumission laws within the general framework of Islamic inheritance jurisprudence.
